Payment Plans And Waivers
Fold It Up

A payment plan spreads what you owe over time and stops collection for as long as you keep it up. The IRS Payment Plan covers every year you owe the IRS: monthly payments on up to $50,000, or everything paid within 180 days with no fee. Each state has its own plan, separate from the IRS’s. Connecticut’s Installment Agreement runs 2 to 12 months on up to $50,000. Interest keeps adding up under every plan.

Where To Find It
Papers, Tax Returns, IRS Payment Plan And Connecticut DRS Installment Agreement.
When You Can Use It
From the guide’s chapter “Cover, Benefits And Returns”. The plan panels show while you owe anything, or once a plan has a history.
Show Me Where
What To Press
On Tax Returns, find the IRS Payment Plan panel. Under Plan Type, choose Monthly Payments or Paid Within 180 Days.
For monthly payments, type an amount in Each Month (USD) or leave the lowest one shown, leave By Direct Debit ticked or clear it, read the setup fee below, and press Apply.
For a state, use its own panel, such as Connecticut DRS Installment Agreement: choose the months under Pay Over and press Apply For The Plan.
If you miss a payment, press Catch Up on the plan’s panel. To change a monthly IRS plan, type a New Monthly Payment (USD) and press Revise The Plan.
Under a year with Oregon’s three-year penalty, press Ask For Its Waiver.
What You Need First
Something owed to that authority, and every return past its due date filed.
For the IRS: less than $100,000 for the short-term plan, or $50,000 or less for monthly payments, with each month at least what you owe spread over 72 months.
For Connecticut: up to $50,000, over 2 to 12 months, with no year it has levied still owed. A year a levy paid off doesn’t count.
To catch up, a plan with a missed payment. To revise, a monthly IRS plan that’s in force or behind.
TIME AND MONEY
Time
None
IRS Setup Fee, Monthly
$29 by direct debit, $69 without. If your latest return shows income of at most 250% of that year’s poverty line, or you have no return yet, $0 by direct debit or $43 without
IRS Short-Term Plan
No fee
Revising An IRS Plan
$6
Connecticut’s Plan
No fee
The IRS’s Lowest Monthly Payment
What you owe spread over 72 months (estimated)
How Often A Payment Is Taken
Every 30 days from approval, from your accounts
What Happens
STRAIGHT AWAY
Once you apply, the IRS plan reads Being decided, and the IRS’s letters stop.
Once it’s approved, the setup fee leaves your bank. On a return filed on time, each month of late-payment penalty that begins from then on is 0.25%; the month already begun stays at 0.5%.
Connecticut decides at once, stops its letters, and files no lien while the plan is in force.
Catch Up pays the missed payment now (everything you owe, on a short-term plan) and puts the plan back in force.
Revise The Plan pays its $6 fee and sets the new monthly payment on everything you owe. A plan that was behind is back in force, the missed payment left in what you owe, and its next payment comes 30 days later.
A waiver takes its share off the three-year penalty, or refunds it if the year is already paid.
LATER ON
A monthly plan takes its payment every 30 days, oldest year first. A short-term plan takes everything you owe on its 180th day.
If your bank can’t cover a payment, Notice CP523 gives you 30 days to catch up. After that the plan ends, and five weeks later the IRS sends its final notice before a levy.
New tax while a monthly plan is in force joins it if it’s no more than two payments’ worth. More than that brings Notice CP523 and 30 days to revise the plan before it ends.
Connecticut ends its plan at the first missed payment. DRS publishes no rule for this, so that part is the game’s. 30 days later it sends “Connecticut DRS Intends To Levy” and files its lien. New York allows until the next due date and California gives a 30-day notice, and for those Catch Up appears.
Paid off, a plan ends as Paid in full.
If the IRS declines a plan, it reads Declined, a notice says why, and the IRS’s letters on what you still owe start again from the step they had reached.
READING THE RESULT
The panel’s subtitle is the plan’s status: Being decided, In force, A payment missed, Ended, Paid in full or Declined, for the IRS’s plan and a state’s alike.
Covers is what the plan took in when it began, or when it was last revised. Each Month and Next Payment are what it takes and when. While a plan is being decided, Answered By gives the day you’ll hear.
By Direct Debit changes the setup fee and the words beside Each Month. Either way, every plan payment is taken from your accounts on its day.
The Plan’s History lists every payment, missed payment and change.
Under a plan, a year’s balance still grows by its interest, so a longer plan costs more in total.
A Connecticut plan has no Catch Up, and Oregon’s waiver is only for a year you owed Oregon. A life lived in New Haven files in Connecticut, so it meets neither.
How It Connects
COMES FIRST
Your Tax Return: Every return past its due date has to be filed before the IRS or a state sets up a plan.
CHANGES STRAIGHT AWAY
Paying Tax Owed: A plan being decided or in force stops the letters and the levy on what you owe.
A Tax Lien: While a state plan is in force, no lien is filed, and one that was only announced comes to nothing.
CHANGES LATER
Your Accounts: Each plan payment is taken from your accounts on its day, every 30 days.
WORTH DOING WITH IT
Permission To Work: A Social Security number gets an IRS plan decided within a minute. Without one it takes 30 days.
WHAT LEADS HERE
Paying Tax Owed: When you can’t pay at once, a plan stops collection for as long as you keep it up.
A Tax Lien: While a state plan is in force, no lien is filed. Connecticut files its lien at its second notice.
Permission To Work: With a number, the IRS decides a plan within a minute. Without one, it’s by mail in 30 days.
What To Do Next
Keep each payment in your checking account or savings on its day, every 30 days.
If you can pay more, use Pay on the year’s panel to finish sooner: interest keeps adding up while the plan runs.
Once a year is paid off, check for a lien under it: see A Tax Lien.
If You Can’t
Apply shows while you owe the IRS and have no IRS plan being decided, in force or behind.
Apply, for monthly payments: “Your bank can’t cover the … setup fee, so you haven’t applied and nothing was charged.” Applied for by mail, a plan is declined on its decision day if your bank can’t pay the fee then.
“The IRS needs every return filed first, and your … return isn’t. File it first.”
A short-term plan for $100,000 or more: “A short-term plan is for less than ….” A Simple Payment Plan over $50,000: a larger balance needs a financial statement, which the game doesn’t offer.
“The lowest monthly payment is …: what you owe, spread over 72 months.”
For a state, each refusal names its agency, such as Connecticut DRS: “… needs every return filed first, and your … return isn’t. File it first.”, a balance over its limit, months outside its range (“… sets up a plan over 2 to 12 months.”), a plan already applied for or in force (“You already have a plan with ….”), or a year it has levied that’s still owed.
Catch Up shows only while a plan is behind, and your bank has to cover the payment: “Your bank can’t cover …, so nothing was paid.” On a plan that isn’t behind: “Your plan isn’t behind, so there’s nothing to catch up.”, or for a state’s plan, which Connecticut ends rather than lets fall behind, “That plan isn’t behind, so there’s nothing to catch up.”
Revise The Plan shows only on a monthly IRS plan in force or behind. It refuses a payment under the lowest monthly payment, more than $50,000 owed now, or a $6 fee your bank can’t cover.
Ask For Its Waiver: “There’s no three-year penalty on that year.”, “Its waiver has already been decided.”, “File your own return for the year first.”, or more than a year since full payment.
MISTAKES, AND PUTTING THEM RIGHT
Setting a monthly payment your accounts can’t keep: a missed one brings CP523 at once. Keep the payment in your checking account or savings on its day.
Applying with no Social Security number and paying nothing meanwhile: the IRS answers a mailed Form 9465 in 30 days, and interest runs the whole time.
Taking the IRS’s plan for a state’s: it covers federal tax only. Apply to Connecticut for its own.
Missing a Connecticut payment: its plan ends at once, where the IRS gives you 30 days. Pay the year off with Pay if you can.
What Decides It
A Social Security Number
With one, the IRS decides an online application within a minute. Without one, Form 9465 goes by mail and is answered in 30 days
Your Latest Return
Its income decides whether you pay the IRS’s low-income fee
Every Year Owed
One IRS plan covers them all, paying the oldest first
When Each Return Was Filed
The IRS’s late-payment penalty falls to 0.25% for each month that begins under a plan only on a return filed on time
Oregon’s Waiver Schedule
70% of the penalty if your return came before any notice, 50% after a demand, and 25% after an assessment
A Worked Example

You owe the IRS $1,800 across two years. Every return is filed, the later one in February before it was due. You have a Social Security number, and your latest return’s income is under 250% of the poverty line.

Choose Monthly Payments, leave Each Month at its lowest and By Direct Debit ticked, and press Apply.
Keep the payment in your checking account each month.

What comes of it. It’s approved within a minute, with no setup fee at the low-income rate: $25 a month, the $1,800 over 72 months, with the first payment 30 days later. The IRS’s letters stop. On both years’ returns, filed on time, each month of penalty that begins under the plan is 0.25% instead of 0.5%: on the earlier year from its next month (the month already begun stays at 0.5%), and on the later year from its first month past its due date. Interest keeps adding up, so paying more with Pay shortens the plan.

Your Tax Return
Fold It Up

Your tax return settles a year’s income tax with the IRS and your state. The game prepares it for you each February 1 from what you earned, what was withheld and where you lived, and you send it with File It. Filed by the deadline, April 15 or the next business day (June 15 for a 1040-NR with no wages on it), it costs only the tax. Filed late with tax owed, the IRS adds penalties and interest. A refund comes 21 days later, the IRS’s and Connecticut’s alike, though the IRS’s takes 70 on a 1040-NR filed without a Social Security number.

Where To Find It
Papers, Tax Returns, Each Year’s Return Panel.
When You Can Use It
From the guide’s chapter “Cover, Benefits And Returns”. Each year’s return is ready on February 1 of the next year, if there’s one to file.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Papers, then the Tax Returns tab. Each year has a panel headed with the year, showing Due and its date, or Filed once it’s in.
Read its lines: your wages, interest and any scholarship for living costs, the tax on them and what was withheld. The last line says You Owe or Your Refund.
Press File It, on the panel or on the year’s item in What Needs You. If the IRS has filed one for you, the button reads File Your Own In Its Place.
To correct a year you’ve filed, press Amend The Return…, then File The Amendment. Not Now leaves it as it is.
What You Need First
A return for the year. You get one each February 1 for a year where you owe tax, are due a refund (including Canada’s), or had income of at least a single filer’s standard deduction ($16,100 for 2026). A student on an F-1 gets one every year they’re here, for Form 8843.
To pay a balance when you file, enough in your checking account and savings for each authority’s part. The IRS’s part and each state’s are taken separately, each whole or not at all.
To amend: a return you filed yourself, within 3 years of filing or 2 of your last payment on it, with no amendment already being processed.
TIME AND MONEY
Time
None: filing and amending don’t move the clock
A Balance
Taken from your checking account when you file, then from savings at the same bank. Each authority’s part is paid in full or not at all
Filing Late With A Balance
5% of the IRS’s part for each month or part of a month, for the first five months: 0.5% of it for paying late and the rest for filing late. After that, 0.5% a month for paying late alone, until that share reaches 25%. After 60 days the filing share is at least $535, or the IRS’s whole part if that’s less
Interest
7% a year, compounded daily, from the due date, on the IRS’s part and on the filing-late share of the penalty
An Amendment
No fee
An Amendment’s Wait
10 weeks before the IRS processes it (the IRS says eight to twelve) (estimated)
What Happens
STRAIGHT AWAY
The panel reads Filed with the date, and the year’s item in What Needs You is answered.
Any balance your checking account and savings can cover is paid at once, to the IRS and to each state separately. A part they can’t cover stays owed, and the panel shows what you still owe each one.
Filed late with a balance owed to the IRS, a Late Penalties line shows what filing late added. A state’s own late penalty is under its Penalties, in Owed To and the state’s agency.
An IRS refund shows as Refund Arrives, with its date. A state refund shows under Who It’s Owed To.
An amendment shows on the panel with its form, the date you filed it, how much more or less tax it means (or “no change in the total”, with each side that moved), and an estimate of when the IRS will process it. Once processed, the same line gives the date, with any refund and its interest.
LATER ON
An IRS refund is paid into your checking account 21 days after filing, or 70 days on a 1040-NR filed without a Social Security number. The IRS first takes from it anything you owe for another year, then any past-due tax you owe a state.
If you leave a balance owing, the IRS’s bill, Notice CP14, comes when you file, and its reminders start five weeks after the deadline, or after filing if that’s later. Connecticut’s bill comes 30 days after the deadline, or after filing if that’s later. See Paying Tax Owed. With an IRS plan in force, a new IRS balance goes into the plan instead. Connecticut’s deadline is mid-April, even on a 1040-NR the IRS takes in June.
If it’s still unfiled on the deadline, a notice tells you the return is late.
If it’s unfiled and you owe the IRS, Notice CP2566 comes 365 days after the deadline (when is estimated) with the IRS’s own figures, which leave out the foreign tax credit and the premium tax credit that only your return can claim. 120 days later it’s assessed, with its penalty and interest, and collected.
Past its deadline and unfiled with a balance, it weighs on you each day, the way tax owed does. See Paying Tax Owed.
If you owe Connecticut, DRS acts on its own part: its notice that it made your return comes 92 days after the deadline (estimated, since DRS doesn’t say when it acts), and 60 days later it’s assessed, with a penalty of at least $50.
An amendment is processed 10 weeks after you file it. More tax is added, with interest from the due date. Less tax comes off what you owe, and the rest is refunded with the IRS’s interest.
READING THE RESULT
The You Owe or Your Refund line covers the whole year, the IRS and the state together. Once it’s filed, Who It’s Owed To splits it: the IRS’s line, then each state’s.
A balance on a return filed on time means the year’s withholding and credits fell short of the tax. A refund means they came to more.
Filed by the IRS in the heading means the IRS assessed the year without you. If you file your own return instead, the tax becomes what your return says, the penalty and interest fall in proportion, and anything you paid beyond your own return’s tax comes back at once.
Late Penalties is what filing late added on the day you filed. What the IRS charges after that grows under Penalties in Owed To The IRS.
How It Connects
CHANGES STRAIGHT AWAY
Your Accounts: Filing takes any balance from your accounts at once, the checking account first and then savings.
What Needs You: Filing answers the year’s item in What Needs You.
Papers: The Papers line on Home says when an unfiled return is due, what filing it would pay (including any late penalty), and the tax you owe.
CHANGES LATER
Paying Tax Owed: A balance your bank couldn’t pay at filing stays owed: the IRS’s bill comes at once, and its first reminder five weeks after the deadline, or after filing if that’s later.
Your Accounts: A refund is paid into your checking account 21 days after filing, or 70 days on a 1040-NR filed without a Social Security number.
WORTH DOING WITH IT
Permission To Work: On a 1040-NR, having a Social Security number before you file saves the seven weeks an ITIN application holds up the refund.
WHAT LEADS HERE
What Needs You: Your return’s question carries File It, which files the year’s return as Papers would.
What You Owe The School: Grant aid is a taxable scholarship, kept for the year’s tax return.
Work-Study Shifts: Work-study wages are income on the year’s tax return.
Cabaret And Summer Cabaret: The summer stipend is wages on the year’s tax return, with its tax already withheld.
A Bank At Home: Each February’s return reports its interest by its country, and a US citizen is told there about the FBAR and Form 8938.
Papers: The Tax Returns tab holds each year’s return, ready each February for a year where you owe tax or are due a refund, or had income of the standard deduction or more, and every year for a student on an F-1.
Health Cover: Each marketplace premium paid is kept for the year’s premium tax credit, which the return works out.
Unemployment And Assistance: What a claim pays is kept as the year’s unemployment insurance, income on your return.
Pensions: A pension paid is kept as the year’s pension income, and Social Security is taxed on the return as IRC 86 says.
Paying Tax Owed: You owe a balance only on a filed return, or on one the IRS or a state assessed without you.
Payment Plans And Waivers: Every return past its due date has to be filed before the IRS or a state sets up a plan.
A Tax Lien: A lien is withdrawn as filed in error only after your own return has replaced the assessment it was filed on.
Permission To Work: A 1040-NR filed without a number goes in with an ITIN application, which holds up its refund seven weeks longer.
What To Do Next
If the panel shows a balance still owed, pay it or set up a plan: see Paying Tax Owed and Payment Plans And Waivers.
If a refund is coming, watch for Refund Arrives on the panel and the money in your checking account.
On an F-1 without a Social Security number, apply for one before next year’s return: see Permission To Work.
If You Can’t
A year with nothing owed or due back, and income under the year’s standard deduction ($16,100 for 2026), has no return and so no File It. A student on an F-1 always has one.
File It shows only on a year you haven’t filed, or one the IRS filed, where it reads File Your Own In Its Place. To change a year you’ve filed, amend it.
Amend The Return… is grayed out with its reason beside it: “An amended return for this year is already with the IRS.”, or the date the time to amend it ran out. A year the IRS filed shows no Amend The Return…: file your own return in its place first.
File The Amendment: “Your return as filed matches what’s on record, so there’s nothing to amend.” Nothing about the year has changed since you filed.
Until you’ve read the guide’s chapter “Cover, Benefits And Returns”, File It shows as Locked.
MISTAKES, AND PUTTING THEM RIGHT
Waiting past the deadline because your bank is short. After 60 days the IRS’s filing share is at least $535, or the whole IRS part if that’s less, and a state charges its own. File on time anyway: what goes unpaid then grows only by the late-payment share and interest.
Looking for the item in What Needs You after the deadline: it lapses on the day, but File It stays on the Papers panel for as long as the year is unfiled.
Leaving the IRS’s own return in place: it leaves out the foreign tax credit and the premium tax credit. File Your Own In Its Place replaces it, even after it’s been assessed.
What Decides It
Your Year’s Record
Wages and what was withheld from them, bank interest, any taxable scholarship, unemployment insurance and a pension, as recorded through the year
Where You Lived
The town you last lived in that year decides the state’s tax and any city’s
Your Citizenship
A student on an F-1 files Form 1040-NR with Form 8843, on US income only, so bank interest isn’t taxed
Your Health Cover
Months on a marketplace plan count toward the premium tax credit and Connecticut’s premium assistance
A Social Security Number
On a 1040-NR filed without one, an ITIN application holds up the refund for seven weeks more
A Worked Example

Your 2026 return leaves $400 owed to the IRS, due April 15, 2027, and your accounts can cover what filing takes.

Press File It by April 15, 2027.
Or wait, and press it 85 days late, on July 9, 2027.

What comes of it. On time, it costs the $400 and nothing more. On July 9, 2027, the IRS adds $406 of late penalties, $400 for filing late and $6 for paying late (after 60 days the filing share is at least $400, the whole balance, since that’s under $535), and about $13.15 of interest: $819.15 in all.

Paying Tax Owed
Fold It Up

If your bank couldn’t pay all your tax when you filed, the rest stays owed in three parts: the tax, the penalties and the interest. The last two keep growing by each authority’s rules. Pay takes any part of it from your bank now, or all of it if you leave the box blank. If you don’t pay, the IRS levies your accounts 170 days after the deadline, and Connecticut 90 days after it, each counted from filing if that’s later.

Where To Find It
Papers, Tax Returns, Owed To The IRS And Owed To A State.
When You Can Use It
From the guide’s chapter “Cover, Benefits And Returns”, once a filed year has a balance left owing.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Papers, then Tax Returns, and find the year’s panel. Owed To The IRS shows Tax Unpaid, Penalties and Interest as of now.
Type an amount in Pay (Blank Pays It All), or leave it blank, and press Pay.
A state has its own box under Owed To and its agency’s name, such as Pay Connecticut (Blank Pays It All), with its own Pay.
Payments On The Year, and Payments To each state, list every payment, levy and refund offset with how it was split.
What You Need First
A filed year with a balance still owed to that authority, or a year a state assessed without your return.
The amount in your checking account and savings. A payment is taken whole or not at all, from the checking account first and then savings.
TIME AND MONEY
Time
None
Money
Whatever you choose to pay, up to what you owe now
The IRS’s Interest
7% a year, compounded daily (a 366th of it a day in a leap year), on the tax, the penalties and the interest. It runs from the due date on the tax and on a late return’s filing-late share. On that return’s paying-late share it runs only once that share is still unpaid 21 days after the filing or the IRS’s assessment, and then from that day. On each month’s penalty after that, it runs from when the penalty is added
The IRS’s Late-Payment Penalty
0.5% of the unpaid tax for each month or part of a month since the due date, up to 25% in all. On a return filed late, the months up to filing (including the month it was filed) are charged with filing, count toward the 25%, and aren’t charged again. On a return filed on time, it’s 0.25% for each month that begins while a payment plan is in force
Connecticut’s Penalty
10% of the tax still unpaid after its due date, charged once. The due date is mid-April, even on a 1040-NR due in June
Connecticut’s Interest
1% for each month or part of a month from that date, worked out to the cent each month, on the tax alone
What Happens
STRAIGHT AWAY
The amount leaves your bank, and a message says how it was split between the tax, penalties and interest, and what you still owe.
The IRS’s monthly penalty is a share of the tax still unpaid, so paying down the tax lowers every later month of it.
Paid in full, the year’s remaining letters are canceled, and any lien on it reads Paid: Release To Come.
If you pay off everything you owe a state outside its plan, the plan ends as paid.
LATER ON
If you left a balance at filing, the IRS’s bill, Notice CP14, comes at once. On a return filed before the deadline it names the deadline, and nothing is added before then. Notice CP501 comes five weeks after the deadline, or after filing if that’s later, then CP503, CP504 and the LT11 final notice, each five weeks after the one before. 30 days after the LT11, the IRS levies your checking account and savings for what they hold, and again every 91 days while you owe anything (how often is estimated).
Connecticut sends “A Bill From Connecticut DRS” 30 days after the deadline, or after filing if that’s later (its deadline is mid-April, even on a 1040-NR the IRS takes in June), and “Connecticut DRS Intends To Levy” 30 days after that, filing its lien then. 30 days later it levies, and again every 91 days (these timings are estimated, since DRS doesn’t publish its own).
If you owe the IRS $10,000 or more on the year at its final notice, it files a Notice Of Federal Tax Lien. See A Tax Lien.
A federal refund from another year goes first to what you owe the IRS, then to past-due tax you owe a state. A Connecticut refund goes first to what you owe Connecticut.
While you owe tax, or a return is past its deadline and unfiled with a balance, each day ends with 4 more points of stress and 2 fewer of morale, scaled by your temperament. It’s the same worry any money trouble brings, felt once a day however many troubles there are.
READING THE RESULT
Tax Unpaid, Penalties and Interest are as of now. The Still Owed line in the year’s table is their total.
The note under Penalties gives the rate running: 0.5% a month, or 0.25% for each month that begins while an IRS plan is in force on a return filed on time. A state’s note gives its own rule.
A state whose notes read “None added: the game doesn’t have this state’s rules” keeps its balance with no penalty or interest, because its collection rules aren’t in the game.
In a list of payments, “taken by levy” is a levy, and “kept from a refund” is a refund kept for what you owe, whether another year’s or an amended return’s, in the IRS’s list and a state’s alike. A state’s list also reads “paid through the payment plan” for its plan’s payments.
How It Connects
COMES FIRST
Your Tax Return: You owe a balance only on a filed return, or on one the IRS or a state assessed without you.
CHANGES STRAIGHT AWAY
Your Accounts: Each payment leaves your accounts at once, the checking account first and then savings.
A Tax Lien: Paying a year in full moves its lien to Paid: Release To Come.
How You Are: Tax owed weighs on you: each day ends with more stress and less morale until it’s paid.
CHANGES LATER
Your Accounts: If you leave it owing, a levy takes what your accounts hold on its day.
WORTH DOING WITH IT
Payment Plans And Waivers: When you can’t pay at once, a plan stops collection for as long as you keep it up.
WHAT LEADS HERE
Your Affairs And What You’re Worth: Tax owed worries you each day like a debt, though it’s on Papers and Owed leaves it out.
Your Tax Return: A balance your bank couldn’t pay at filing stays owed: the IRS’s bill comes at once, and its first reminder five weeks after the deadline, or after filing if that’s later.
Payment Plans And Waivers: A plan being decided or in force stops the letters and the levy on what you owe.
A Tax Lien: A lien is released only once what it was filed for is paid in full.
What To Do Next
If you can’t pay it all soon, apply for a payment plan to stop the letters and the levy: see Payment Plans And Waivers.
Once a year is paid in full, check for a lien under it and ask for its release if the authority needs asking: see A Tax Lien.
If You Can’t
Pay shows only while you owe that authority something on the year.
“Enter an amount above zero.” for nothing or less.
An amount over what you owe: “You owe …. Pay that amount or less.”
“Your bank can’t cover …, so nothing was paid.”: your checking account and savings together hold less than the amount. Pay a smaller part.
MISTAKES, AND PUTTING THEM RIGHT
Waiting for the levy: it takes whatever your checking account and savings hold on the day, up to everything you owe, whatever that money was for.
Watching only the IRS: Connecticut levies 90 days after the deadline, or after filing if that’s later, against the IRS’s 170, so Connecticut levies first.
Holding back because a part won’t clear it: a part paid to the IRS cuts the tax first, and its penalty is a share of the tax left. Connecticut takes its penalty and interest first, so there a part shrinks the tax last.
What Decides It
Where A Partial Payment Goes
To the IRS: the tax, then the penalties, then the interest. To Connecticut DRS: the penalty, then the interest, then the tax, as its statute says
What You Owe Now
Brought up to date the minute you pay, with its interest and penalty included
Your Accounts
Your checking account, and your savings at the same bank, as far as that bank lets money out
A Worked Example

Your 2026 return, filed on time, left $400 of tax owed to the IRS and $200 to Connecticut, and your bank couldn’t pay either.

On May 10, 2027, type 150 in Pay (Blank Pays It All) and press Pay.
Type 100 in Pay Connecticut (Blank Pays It All) and press Pay.

The Doctor And The Pharmacy
Fold It Up

About twice a year a week brings a doctor’s visit, and the game books it for you at your doctor’s practice, at 10:00 AM on a weekday that isn’t a public holiday. In New Haven, while Yale Health covers you, that’s Yale Health Center, Student Health, the next weekday, for $0, unless you pick Fair Haven Community Health Care, 24 days on at the uninsured price. Once Yale Health no longer covers you, it’s Fair Haven Community Health Care, 24 days on. Keep the appointment and you’re seen and billed your share. Miss it and you aren’t seen: press Book An Appointment to book it again. Your Pharmacy sets the cash price a generic is filled at, from Walmart’s $4 against the $40 median of 2019, grown since, and your plan’s copay is never more than that price.

Where To Find It
Papers, Health Cover, Your Doctor.
When You Can Use It
From the guide’s chapter “Cover, Benefits And Returns”. Your Pharmacy is America’s; Fill A Longer Supply shows while you keep a condition up.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Papers, Health Cover. Your Doctor names where a doctor’s visit, urgent care and an emergency are had where you live, and what each would cost you now.
The Your Doctor box picks the practice a visit is booked at; it shows where two practices or more would see you, each with what a visit there costs you and how soon it’s booked. A Yale student Yale Health covers picks between Yale Health Center, Student Health, $0 and the next weekday, and Fair Haven Community Health Care, $183.98 in 2026 and 24 days on. Until you pick, The Practice Your Cover Uses sends a visit to Yale Health Center, Student Health. Once Yale Health no longer covers you there’s one practice for you, Fair Haven Community Health Care, and the line names it.
The Your Pharmacy box, in America, picks the chain whose cash price fills a generic.
A booked appointment shows below with its date. When the clock reaches it, it stops and asks; be awake and out of hospital at the hour.
Call It Off cancels an appointment. The visit stays owed, and Book An Appointment books it again.
Fill A Longer Supply, 90 Days, under Your Long-Term Conditions, fills the medicine of every condition you keep up for that long at once, paid ahead. Where the bank can’t cover every condition’s fill, none is filled.
What You Need First
Your Doctor: a practice in the town you live in that would see you, two or more of them. In New Haven the game has Fair Haven Community Health Care and Yale Health Center, Student Health; Yale Health Center, Student Health sees only Yale students Yale Health covers: while you’re at the School, thirty days after a withdrawal past the fifteenth day of classes, not after one by it, and to July 31 after the degree.
Book An Appointment: a visit owed, missed or called off, and no appointment booked.
Your Pharmacy: living in America.
Fill A Longer Supply: a condition you keep up, its row showing Let It Go, and the bank able to pay every condition’s fill.
TIME AND MONEY
A Visit
Your plan’s copay: $0 on Yale Health at Yale Health Center, Student Health, HUSKY D and Covered Connecticut, $45 on Access Health CT’s silver plan; uninsured, the commercial price times 1.75, $183.98 in 2026. On Yale Health a visit at Fair Haven Community Health Care is billed at that uninsured price: Yale Health pays for a member’s care at its own Health Center, except in an emergency
Time On The Calendar
20 minutes, at 10:00 AM local time on a weekday that isn’t a public holiday where you live (estimated)
A Generic, Uninsured
Walmart $4, Costco $4.10, Kroger $5, CVS $12.50; at any pharmacy, the $40 median of 2019, grown by the drug price index (estimated)
A Longer Supply
Up to 90 days at once in America, at 3 fills’ share, paid then (estimated)
What Happens
STRAIGHT AWAY
Choosing a doctor or a pharmacy sets it at once, and the toast names it: “… is now your doctor.” or “… is now your pharmacy.”
Book An Appointment puts it on the calendar; the toast gives its date, and a notice names the practice.
Call It Off takes it off the calendar, with no toast, and leaves the visit owed: the panel reads “…: not yet seen”.
Fill A Longer Supply pays at once from your checking account, then the easy-access savings at its bank where Savings Covers The Current Account is On, then its overdraft, moves each Medicine until date on by the days filled, and the toast says “90 days of medicine filled.” Where the bank can’t cover every condition’s fill, it’s refused whole, “Your bank can’t cover … for every condition’s fill, so nothing was filled or charged.”, and nothing is filled or paid.
LATER ON
At the hour, kept: “A Doctor’s Visit” comes as a notice, and your share is billed, due in 30 days, under the practice it was booked at; on Yale Health at Yale Health Center, Student Health, HUSKY D or Covered Connecticut that’s $0, and no bill is made. On Yale Health at Fair Haven Community Health Care it’s $183.98 in 2026, and the notice says Yale Health pays for a visit at its own Health Center. On Access Health CT’s silver plan it’s the $45 copay, with no deductible, and Care And Its Bills gives what the plan paid of the visit’s price under Plan Paid. Your prescriptions are renewed, a review visit marks its condition reviewed, and the visit may end in a referral, booked for the specialist’s wait.
At the hour, booked at Yale Health Center, Student Health after Yale Health’s cover has ended: “Not Seen At Your Practice” comes as a notice, the visit goes unbilled and stays owed, and Book An Appointment books it at Fair Haven Community Health Care, for its wait.
At the hour, missed: “Missed The Doctor” comes as a notice, the visit goes unbilled, and it stays owed until you book, or until a Monday brings another visit, which books the one owed.
Booked at Fair Haven Community Health Care while Yale Health didn’t cover you, and Yale Health covering you again before its day (Affiliate cover bought on a leave, or back from the leave): it stays where it was booked, “Your Appointment Is Outside Yale Health” comes as a notice, and its line under Your Doctor says to call it off and Book An Appointment, to be seen at Yale Health Center, Student Health. Kept, it’s billed at Fair Haven Community Health Care’s uninsured price.
Each Monday, a condition’s medicine with 7 days or fewer left is refilled for 30 days: a generic at your pharmacy’s price, a brand at the median.
While an appointment is booked, a new doctor’s visit drawn on a Monday is dropped, never billed, and no condition review is booked. While a visit is owed, no condition review is booked, and the next visit a Monday draws books the one owed, one appointment for both.
READING THE RESULT
“What it would cost you here now” is your share under today’s cover, for a visit, urgent care and an emergency.
Elsewhere, a practice picked that publishes its own price, as Bupa’s pay-as-you-go GP in London does, bills a visit at that price: a public system pays its own practices, not a private GP. A life in New Haven never meets one.
A visit you keep doesn’t change your wellbeing by itself. It renews prescriptions, records a review and may bring a referral. Connecticut sets no date after which a prescription for a medicine that isn’t controlled can no longer be filled (its pharmacy statutes, read on October 15, 2026), so in New Haven a renewal changes no fill, and the visit is mostly its bill.
In New Haven the game has 2 practices. On Yale Health, picking Fair Haven Community Health Care changes both how soon you’re seen and what a visit costs: 24 days on and $183.98 in 2026, against the next weekday and $0 at Yale Health Center, Student Health, since Yale Health pays for a member’s care at its own Health Center. Fair Haven keeps a sliding fee for the uninsured, but publishes none of its amounts, so the game bills the uninsured price there. An emergency is paid wherever it’s had.
An appointment is had where it was booked. One booked at Fair Haven Community Health Care while Yale Health didn’t cover you, on a leave, is kept there and billed the uninsured price even if Yale Health covers you again before the day; Call It Off and Book An Appointment, and it’s at Yale Health Center, Student Health.
How It Connects
CHANGES STRAIGHT AWAY
Health Cover: A visit you keep is billed at once for your share, and its bill joins Care And Its Bills, due in 30 days.
CHANGES LATER
The Calendar: A booked appointment is a commitment on the calendar, 20 minutes at 10:00 AM on a weekday that isn’t a public holiday, and the clock stops at it.
What Needs You: Booking sends “A Doctor’s Appointment” to What Needs You, a missed one “Missed The Doctor”, and a referral “A Referral”.
COUNTS TOWARD
Conditions And Therapy: Your Pharmacy’s cash price is read for every generic fill of a condition’s medicine.
WHAT LEADS HERE
Looking After Yourself: An injury from a run or a workout brings a doctor’s care, and a bill for it.
Health Cover: Your cover decides your share each time you have care: a visit, urgent care, an emergency or a stay.
Conditions And Therapy: A condition kept up books its review as a doctor’s appointment when it falls due.
What To Do Next
If a visit is owed, press Book An Appointment and keep the hour free on its day.
In America, pick the cheapest pharmacy under Your Pharmacy if you fill generics.
If You Can’t
“There’s nothing to see a doctor about.”: no visit is owed.
“You have an appointment already.”
“No waiting time is published where you live, so there’s nothing to book: you’re seen when you need care.”: Ireland’s way, where a visit comes unbooked.
“Your doctor has to be in the town you live in.” or “That isn’t a doctor’s practice.”
“Yale Health sees Yale students it covers, and it doesn’t cover you now.”: Yale Health’s practice sent once its cover has ended; the box doesn’t offer it then.
“You can choose a pharmacy only in the United States.”
Pressed, Fill A Longer Supply says “Your bank can’t cover … for every condition’s fill, so nothing was filled or charged.” when the bank can’t pay every condition’s fill.
Before the chapter is read, the boxes, Call It Off and Book An Appointment are grayed, their tooltip naming the chapter.
MISTAKES, AND PUTTING THEM RIGHT
Looking to go back to The Practice Your Cover Uses, The First Practice In Town or Any Pharmacy, At The Typical Price: each shows only until you pick, so you can change a choice to another practice or chain, but not undo it.
Picking Fair Haven Community Health Care while Yale Health covers you: each visit there is billed $183.98 in 2026, where Yale Health Center, Student Health costs $0. Picking Yale Health Center, Student Health again puts it right for the next visit booked.
Sleeping through 10:00 AM on the day: the appointment is missed. Book An Appointment books again, for the full wait.
Calling an appointment off and leaving it: the visit stays owed, and no condition review is booked, until you book it or a Monday brings another visit.
Filling a longer supply to save: it charges 3 fills’ share at once, the same as 3 ordinary fills. What it buys is medicine paid ahead, which lasts through a month the bank runs too low for Monday’s refill.
What Decides It
The Wait Where You Live
4 days in New York, 13 in Los Angeles, 24 in New Haven: the average of fifteen metros, for a town the survey left out (estimated)
A Practice’s Own Wait
Yale Health Center, Student Health offers a same-day or next-day appointment, and the game books the next weekday; Fair Haven Community Health Care publishes none, and New Haven’s 24 days stand there
Being There
Awake and out of hospital at its hour. An injury that keeps you from class doesn’t keep you from the doctor.
A Referral
9.1% of the visits kept in America end in one, and the specialist is seen 31 days on (estimated)
An Emergency
Keeps you in the department its median time: 189 minutes in Connecticut, at Yale New Haven Hospital, York Street Campus Emergency Department (estimated)
A Worked Example

A student on Yale Health in New Haven, whose Monday brought a doctor’s visit.

A notice: “A doctor’s visit: booked at Yale Health Center, Student Health for …, the usual wait where you live.”, the next weekday.
On the day you sleep past 10:00 AM, and “Missed The Doctor” follows.
Open Papers, Health Cover, and press Book An Appointment beside “A doctor’s visit: not yet seen”.

What comes of it. It’s booked again for the next weekday at Yale Health Center, Student Health, moved to the next working day when that’s a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday where you live, as every booking is. Kept, it costs $0 on Yale Health, renews your prescriptions, and about one time in 11 ends in a referral to a specialist 31 days later.

Health Cover
Fold It Up

Health cover pays for your care. Yale Health covers you while you’re at the School, and the School bills it each term. When it’s about to end, from 60 days before, press Enroll on The Marketplace. If last month’s income is low enough, that takes you into HUSKY D or Covered Connecticut, with no premium. Otherwise it buys Access Health CT’s silver plan, which you can do in open enrollment, in those 60 days, or within 60 days of losing cover. Each piece of care brings a bill for your share, due in 30 days. Under Care And Its Bills you can appeal a denied claim, ask a Connecticut hospital for financial assistance, and pay off anything that went to medical debt.

Where To Find It
Papers, Health Cover: Your Cover, The Marketplace, A Dental Plan, Care And Its Bills.
When You Can Use It
From the guide’s chapter “Cover, Benefits And Returns”. Enroll shows when you may enroll. While Yale Health covers you, that’s only in its last 60 days, once its end is set.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Papers, then Health Cover. Your Cover says what covers you This Month.
Read the line under The Marketplace: it says whether you may enroll now, and why. When Enroll shows beside the title, press it. The toast names what you’re enrolled in and the day it starts.
Once you’re enrolled, Drop The Plan, in the same place, ends a plan of your own at the end of the month.
In Care And Its Bills, each row has its care, its date, Your Share and Due. In the Assistance column, Appeal It answers a denied claim, and Apply For Assistance asks a Connecticut hospital to apply its financial assistance to a bill.
When a bill has gone to medical debt, Pay It Off beside the panel’s title pays all of it.
While Yale Health covers you, A Dental Plan offers Buy Dental: Yale Delta Dental Basic, paid once for Yale’s plan year, to September 30.
What You Need First
Enroll: no plan of your own already, and Yale Health ended, in its last 60 days once its end is set, or lapsed on a personal leave without Affiliate cover.
HUSKY D: last month’s income at or under 138% of the poverty line, $1,835 a month in 2026, and from October 1, 2026 US citizenship or a green card held five years. From January 1, 2027, some of the month before you enroll spent at the School, or $580 of income of any kind in it, or an exception: 65 or over, SNAP received under its work rules, or a stay in hospital you ask for.
Covered Connecticut: last month’s income over HUSKY D’s line and at or under 175% of the year before’s poverty line, $2,282 a month in 2026, and at least 100% of it, since it comes with the premium tax credit; an income HUSKY D’s line takes isn’t Covered Connecticut’s, whatever your status. For a citizen or anyone lawfully present, and from January 1, 2027 for a citizen or a green card holder, not a student in F-1 status or a graduate on OPT.
Apply For HUSKY D: HUSKY D’s income and status met, and its work rules not shown in the month before, with no application of yours waiting. Request A Hardship Exception: a notice of noncompliance waiting on its answer, and a stay in hospital in a month it assessed.
The marketplace: Connecticut’s open enrollment, October 23 to January 15; the 60 days before Yale Health’s cover ends, once its end is set by the degree, a withdrawal or a dismissal; or within 60 days of losing cover, which a plan you dropped or left unpaid isn’t. And not having stayed past your US status.
Appeal It: a denied claim, within 180 days of the care. Apply For Assistance: a Connecticut hospital’s bill for an emergency or a stay, before it’s due.
TIME AND MONEY
Yale Health
Billed by the School each term: your living-expense scholarship meets it where Yale finds need, and otherwise it’s taken from your bank. It leaves you $0 for a visit or urgent care, $50 for the emergency room and $200 an admission to $1,000 a year, $9,100 a year at most
HUSKY D And Covered Connecticut
No premium, and $0 for a visit, urgent care, the emergency room, a stay and a prescription
The Marketplace Premium
The benchmark silver plan, $706 a month in 2026 and $786 a month from 2027, taken in full on the first of each month (estimated)
Access Health CT Standard Silver
$45 a visit, $75 urgent care, $450 the emergency room, a stay $1,500 after a $5,000 deductible, $9,400 a year at most
Uninsured
The commercial price times 1.75: a visit $175 at 2024’s prices and an emergency $4,287.50 at 2019’s, each grown since by its price index. An emergency or a stay at a Connecticut hospital has its financial assistance taken off as it’s billed: free to 250% of the poverty line, 67% off to 550% (estimated)
Yale Delta Dental Basic
$312.72 for Yale’s plan year, paid at once and covering from that day: bought in August or September, to September 30 a year on; bought from October to July, to the next September 30. Cleanings in full, and 80% of a filling paid by the plan after a $50 deductible, to $1,000, both kept by Yale’s plan year, October 1 to September 30: bought in August or September, the weeks before October 1 are the plan year then ending, with a deductible and a maximum of their own
Time
None: enrolling, appealing, applying and paying move no clock
What Happens
STRAIGHT AWAY
Enroll: HUSKY D starts on the first of the month you enroll, and reaches back to the first of an earlier month in which you had care with nothing covering you and HUSKY D would have taken you, three months back for an application in 2026 and one from 2027, the care since priced again as HUSKY D’s; another program or a plan starts on the first of next month. Enrolled before Yale Health’s cover ends, each starts on the first of the month on or after its end, so a graduate’s starts August 1 with no gap. The toast names it and its day.
Drop The Plan: it ends on the first of next month, and no later premium is taken. The toast says “Your plan ends at the end of the month. Dropping it doesn’t open a special enrollment period.”, and the panel says “Dropped: it ends on …” instead of the button. A renewal’s notice of noncompliance waiting on an answer goes with the program it would renew, and so does its decision.
Apply For HUSKY D: the notice “A Notice Of Noncompliance” comes at once, naming the month read, the day to answer by (5 days for it to reach you, then 30 more) and what follows. Applying isn’t being covered: you aren’t covered by HUSKY D yet, and you can still buy a marketplace plan.
Request A Hardship Exception: decided at once. A renewal is renewed, with “Your Public Cover Is Renewed” or, moving from Covered Connecticut, “Your Public Cover Changed At Renewal”; an application is approved, “Public Cover Approved”, from the first of the month you applied in, or of an earlier month with care in it as Enroll reaches back, and a marketplace plan bought meanwhile ends as it begins.
Appeal It: the bill reads Appealed, and its answer comes 60 days on.
Apply For Assistance: decided at once. Free Care clears the bill, 67% Off cuts it, and Over The Limit leaves it as it was. The toast for a bill helped says “The hospital applied its financial assistance to this bill.”
Pay It Off: the whole debt is paid from your checking account, and every bill that went to it reads Settled.
Buy Dental: Yale’s year is paid at once, and the dentist is covered from today.
LATER ON
On the first of each month the marketplace premium is taken from your checking account, then the easy-access savings at its bank where Savings Covers The Current Account is On, then its overdraft. If it can’t be paid, the plan ends that day, and a plan left unpaid opens no special enrollment.
A program comes up for renewal: in Connecticut every 12 months, and from January 1, 2027 every 6. It’s checked on last month’s income again and, for HUSKY D from January 1, 2027, on its work rules in any one of the 6 months before. Kept, the notice “Your Public Cover Is Renewed” says to when, and which month met its work rules, and how. Where last month’s income now places you in the other program, under HUSKY D’s line from Covered Connecticut or over it and within Covered Connecticut’s from HUSKY D, you’re renewed into that one from the same day, with no gap and no premium, and the notice “Your Public Cover Changed At Renewal” says so; into HUSKY D its work rules are asked first. Over every line, or out of the status it asks, it ends at the end of the month at least 10 days on, with the notice “Your Public Cover Ends” naming the day.
Short of HUSKY D’s work rules at a renewal, or on Apply For HUSKY D, “A Notice Of Noncompliance” comes: you have 5 days for it to reach you and 30 more to answer, and a member stays covered meanwhile. Request A Hardship Exception answers it where a month it read had a stay in hospital. Unanswered, it’s decided the day after: a renewal’s cover ends at the end of the month at least 10 days on, with “Your Public Cover Ends”; an application is denied, with “Public Cover Denied”. Either way you can apply again in any month after one that meets the rules, and the marketplace sells to you, without the premium tax credit while HUSKY D would take you but for its work rules.
Covered Connecticut held by a student in F-1 status or a graduate on OPT ends on January 1, 2027, with the notice “Your Public Cover Has Ended”: from then the premium tax credit it comes with is a citizen’s or a green card holder’s. The marketplace still sells to you, with no credit.
Back at the School from a leave, with Yale Health’s student cover again, Covered Connecticut ends at the next month’s start, with the notice “Your Public Cover Has Ended”: it’s for a person with no other cover that counts. HUSKY D stays beside Yale Health, which pays first.
Stay past your US status and, at the next month’s start, a marketplace plan ends with the notice “Your Marketplace Plan Has Ended”, and Covered Connecticut with “Your Public Cover Has Ended”, or, where you enrolled ahead, “Your Marketplace Plan Won’t Begin” and “Your Public Cover Won’t Begin”.
A bill still open on its due date, 30 days on, is taken from your checking account, then the easy-access savings at its bank where Savings Covers The Current Account is On, then its overdraft, if between them they can cover all of it. If not, it’s medical debt, owed to Your Providers, with the notice “A Medical Bill Went Unpaid”.
A medical debt of $500 or more, 365 days after its first bill went unpaid, is reported to your credit record once, at the next month’s start, since you live in Connecticut. The notice is “A Medical Debt Is On Your Record”.
An appeal is decided 60 days on. Overturned, you owe only the plan’s share: what you paid over it comes back into the account your payments go to, what went to debt over it comes off the debt, and what you’d paid toward that debt past what’s left of it comes back too; a debt it clears settles every bill that went to it. Upheld, the bill stands.
Each Monday may bring care at an adult’s rates: about 2 doctor’s visits a year, 0.45 emergency visits, a stay in hospital one year in 25 (3 days), and the flu about one year in 11, likelier when you’re short of sleep or stressed.
On the first of a month that finds you without cover, a notice says “Your Health Cover Ended”, beginning “You’re uncovered from …” and the day your last cover ended. Your 60 days to enroll run from that day: Yale Health’s own end, after the degree August 1, after a withdrawal thirty days from it, which can be weeks before the notice; a program’s at its renewal, at a month’s end; and Yale Health canceled back in time, by a withdrawal by the fifteenth day of classes or a leave begun before them, from the day it was canceled. Told on the day, the notice says “You have 60 days to enroll in the marketplace”; told later, it names the last day, “You can enroll in the marketplace until …”; and where last month’s income qualifies you for HUSKY D or Covered Connecticut, that it takes you at any time, with no premium. A plan you dropped or left unpaid opens no such days, and the notice says the way back is open enrollment, or a month’s income that qualifies you for HUSKY D or Covered Connecticut. Out of status, it says neither the marketplace nor Covered Connecticut will take you.
Yale Delta Dental Basic runs to its September 30 whatever happens to Yale Health, through August and September after the degree too. Paid for the year, it can’t be dropped.
READING THE RESULT
Your Cover, This Month, reads None, in amber, when nothing covers you.
The subtitle of Care And Its Bills shows what you’ve paid this year toward the year’s most; past it, your plan leaves you nothing more for care. HUSKY D and Covered Connecticut have no most: care costs you nothing on them, a prescription costs only its copay where the program has one, and the subtitle says only what you’ve paid.
In the bills table, Due shows a date, Settled, Owed As Debt or Credited. A change of cover back in time, a withdrawal by the fifteenth day of classes or Affiliate cover bought on a leave, leaves each bill as it was issued and adds a line of its own: more owed is billed on it; less owed reads below nothing, Credited, and comes off the bill still open first, which then shows what’s left of the share it was issued at; and Plan Paid on the line is the plan’s change, below nothing where the plan took its part back. A prescription filled in that time is priced again the same way, its line Credited with what comes back to the account your payments go to, or billed with what more is owed. In Assistance, Assistance Taken Off means the hospital screened an uninsured bill when it was billed and took something off it; over 550% of the poverty line it took off nothing, and the bill reads Over The Limit.
The toast after Enroll, Your Cover and the subtitle of Care And Its Bills each name a program by its own name, HUSKY D or Covered Connecticut. The marketplace’s plan reads Marketplace Plan in Your Cover, and Access Health CT Standard Silver over the bills.
The Marketplace says Medicaid’s work rules, HUSKY D’s here, are met from 2027 by a month you spend any of at the School, or one with $580 of income: the one before you apply, and any of the 6 before a renewal. Income of any kind counts toward the $580, interest, a benefit and a pension as pay does.
A marketplace premium is paid in full. The return gives back what’s over your share of income, for an income over 138%, or from 100% where your status keeps you from HUSKY D, and up to 400% of the poverty line; on a 1040-NR too, in 2026, and from 2027 only for a citizen or a green card holder.
How It Connects
COMES FIRST
Leave, Withdrawal And Coming Back: Yale Health covers you while you’re at the School; the degree, a withdrawal, a dismissal or a personal leave without Affiliate cover ends it. A withdrawal by the fifteenth day of a term’s classes, or such a leave, ends the cover then or back to its insurance term’s start, and Enroll waits for the first of the next month, unless it’s open enrollment or last month’s income qualifies you for HUSKY D or Covered Connecticut. Otherwise Enroll shows from 60 days before the cover’s end: at once after a dismissal or any other withdrawal.
CHANGES LATER
Your Affairs And What You’re Worth: A bill unpaid at its due date goes to Owed For Medical Care, a debt your net worth counts; at $500 or more, 365 days on, it marks your credit record.
COUNTS TOWARD
The Doctor And The Pharmacy: Your cover decides your share each time you have care: a visit, urgent care, an emergency or a stay.
Conditions And Therapy: A condition’s month of care and each fill of its medicine are priced at your plan’s copays.
KEPT IN YOUR RECORD
What You Owe The School: The Yale Health plan is billed each term with the School’s charges: the living-expense scholarship meets it where need is found, and your bank pays it where none is.
Your Tax Return: Each marketplace premium paid is kept for the year’s premium tax credit, which the return works out.
WORTH DOING WITH IT
Calling In Sick: A stay in hospital excuses you from school of itself; down with the flu, Call In Sick excuses the day.
WHAT LEADS HERE
Leave, Withdrawal And Coming Back: A personal leave ends Yale Health’s student cover, and Affiliate cover keeps it.
Papers: The Health Cover tab holds your cover, your doctor, your conditions and your medical bills.
The Doctor And The Pharmacy: A visit you keep is billed at once for your share, and its bill joins Care And Its Bills, due in 30 days.
Permission To Work: Your status ends on a set day. Once you’re out of status, a marketplace plan ends at the end of the month.
What To Do Next
Before Yale Health ends, enroll ahead so your new cover starts the day after it, with no gap.
Keep enough in your checking account on the first of each month for a marketplace premium.
If a claim is denied or a hospital bill comes, use Appeal It or Apply For Assistance before its due date.
If You Can’t
“You’re already enrolled.”, or “You’re already enrolled, from ….”: one plan at a time.
“Yale Health covers you while you’re at the School.”: Enroll stays off the screen while you study, unless a personal leave without Affiliate cover lapses it.
“Yale Health covers you until …. You can enroll from …, 60 days before that cover ends.”
“It’s outside open enrollment, … to …, and you haven’t lost cover in the last 60 days.”
Stayed past your US status: the marketplace sells only to a citizen or a person lawfully present.
HUSKY D, its work rules not shown: “From January 1, 2027, … asks for … in the month before you apply, and last month had none of them.”, naming HUSKY D and what it asks: $580.00 of income, time at the School or an exception. The line goes on to say whether the marketplace is open to you, and Enroll shows only where it is, and buys its plan; Apply For HUSKY D, beside it, takes the application on a notice.
“Your application waits on its notice: answer it by …”: one application at a time. “Last month meets its work rules, so press Enroll instead.”: Apply For HUSKY D is for a month that doesn’t.
“There’s no notice of noncompliance waiting for an answer.”, “The … days to answer ended on ….” or “None of the months it checked, …, had a stay in hospital, the one hardship the game counts.”: Request A Hardship Exception doesn’t show, and the notice’s line says which.
“You have no plan of your own to drop.”, or, dropped already, “It’s already dropped, and it ends on ….”
“…, so there’s no renewal left to answer.”, saying the program has ended or the day it ends: a renewal’s notice whose program has ended some other way, and Request A Hardship Exception doesn’t show.
“That claim wasn’t denied.”, “It’s been appealed.” or “An appeal has to be filed within 180 days of the denial, and that time has passed.”: Appeal It doesn’t show.
“Only a Connecticut hospital’s bill can be put in for its financial assistance.”, “It’s already settled or past its due date.”, “The hospital’s financial assistance has already come off it.” or “It’s already been put in for the hospital’s financial assistance.”, for a bill applied for or screened over the limit at billing: Apply For Assistance doesn’t show.
“You owe nothing for care.”, or, when your checking account holds less than the debt, “… has only … of the …, so nothing was paid. Move money into it first, on your bank’s Move Money.” (“… has nothing to pay it with, so nothing was paid.” where it holds nothing).
A Dental Plan shows only while Yale Health covers you or a Yale plan you bought runs: once Yale Health ends, New Haven sells none. Pressed, Buy Dental says “Your bank can’t cover … for the year, so nothing was charged.” when the bank can’t pay the year.
Prepay Three Months and Prepay A Year are England’s, for its £9.90 prescription charge: “The prepayment certificate is only for England’s prescription charge.” A life in New Haven never sees them.
MISTAKES, AND PUTTING THEM RIGHT
Waiting for Yale’s cover to end before enrolling: after the degree Yale Health runs to July 31, and Enroll shows from June 2. Enrolled by July 31, cover begins August 1 with no gap; enrolled on August 1 or later, a plan begins the first of the next month, and August goes uncovered, where HUSKY D, if last month’s income and its work rules take you, begins on August 1 all the same.
Letting the checking account run dry before the first: the premium isn’t taken, the plan ends, and a plan left unpaid opens no special enrollment. Unless a month’s income qualifies you for HUSKY D or Covered Connecticut, you wait for open enrollment, October 23 to January 15.
Leaving a bill to its due date with too little in the bank: it goes to medical debt. Pay It Off takes the whole debt from your checking account at once, so wait until it holds all of it.
Missing a denial: “A Claim Denied” comes as a notice, and an appeal is filed within 180 days of the care.
Dropping cover to save the premium: care uninsured is billed at 1.75 times the commercial price, less a Connecticut hospital’s financial assistance for an emergency or a stay, and a marketplace plan dropped can’t be bought again until open enrollment.
Buying Yale’s dental plan late in its year: bought from October to July, it runs only to the next September 30, so bought in June or July the full year’s premium buys a summer. Bought in August or September, it runs from that day to September 30 a year on.
What Decides It
Last Month’s Income
All the income your record holds for the calendar month before, against the poverty line: wages and work-study’s pay, and the unemployment benefit, interest and pensions paid that month too
The Work Rules’ Months
For HUSKY D’s work rules: the calendar month before you enroll, and at renewal any one of the 6 calendar months before the renewal’s. A month meets them with any of it spent at the School (the month you leave it, on a leave, by withdrawing or with the degree, counts whole, and so does the month you come back), $580 of income of any kind (pay, an unemployment benefit, interest or a pension), being 65 or over for any of it, SNAP received in it while you were under SNAP’s work rules (out of school, no unemployment claim, 18 to 64), or a stay in hospital in it, if you ask
Your Status
US citizenship or five years with a green card for HUSKY D from October 1, 2026; lawful presence for the marketplace, and for Covered Connecticut until 2027, when it’s a citizen’s or a green card holder’s
A Denied Claim
20% of a marketplace plan’s claims, billed as if you were uninsured; insurers uphold 56% of appeals (estimated)
The Hospital’s Financial Assistance
Your last twelve months’ income against the poverty line: free to 250%, 67% off to 550%
Medical Debt On Your Record
$500 or more, unpaid 365 days, and you living outside New York and California
A Worked Example

A US citizen in New Haven who graduated in the spring of 2027, with no pay in July.

On August 1 a notice says “Your Health Cover Ended”.
Open Papers, Health Cover. Under The Marketplace: “From January 1, 2027, HUSKY D asks for $580.00 of income, time at the School or an exception in the month before you apply, and last month had none of them. The marketplace is open to you, because you’re within 60 days of losing cover.”
Press Enroll.

What comes of it. The toast says “Enrolled in the marketplace, from September 1, …”. From September 1 its premium is taken on each month’s first, and a visit costs $45. Care in August, uncovered, is billed at the uninsured price, less the hospital’s financial assistance on an emergency or a stay. Enrolled ahead, from June 2 while Yale Health still covered them, their cover would have begun August 1.

Conditions And Therapy
Fold It Up

A long-term condition is an illness that stays with you: depression, asthma, high blood pressure, diabetes or arthritis. Your Long-Term Conditions, on Health Cover, is where you keep each one up or let it go. Kept up, each costs its month of care and its medicine, at what your plan doesn’t cover. Let It Go stops both, and from then the condition, left untreated, takes its toll each week. With depression, a course of eight therapy sessions can lift it for good.

Where To Find It
Papers, Health Cover, Your Long-Term Conditions.
When You Can Use It
From the guide’s chapter “Cover, Benefits And Returns”. Your Long-Term Conditions shows when you have a long-term condition or wear lenses, and Therapist when you have depression.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Papers, Health Cover, Your Long-Term Conditions. Each row reads Kept Up, Left Untreated, Out Of Medicine, or Kept Up, But This Month’s Care Went Unpaid, with the date your medicine lasts to.
Let It Go stops a condition’s care and its medicine. Keep It Up starts them again.
With depression, pick a Therapist where you live and press Begin A Course Of 8 Sessions. In New Haven that’s Yale Mental Health & Counseling, Free With Yale Health, or Adna Linden Psychotherapy, $240 A Session.
While the course runs, the panel reads “Therapy with …: 2 of 8 sessions”, naming Yale Mental Health & Counseling, and so on. Each session is a commitment the clock stops at.
What You Need First
A long-term condition: drawn once when a life begins; one that begins later comes with a “Diagnosed” notice and is kept up from the start.
Begin A Course Of 8 Sessions: depression, no course running, a therapist in the town you’re in, and for Yale Mental Health & Counseling, Yale Health covering you.
TIME AND MONEY
Depression, A Month
2 therapy sessions at your plan’s visit copay ($0 on Yale Health, $90 a month on Access Health CT silver; uninsured, $139 a session at 2024’s price), and a generic each fill (estimated)
Asthma
A brand inhaler each fill, and a visit’s copay in about two months of twelve (estimated)
High Blood Pressure
A generic each fill
Diabetes
Type 1: insulin, never more than $35 a fill ($25 on Access Health CT’s silver plan, which Connecticut regulates, and $0 on HUSKY D and Covered Connecticut), and a glucose monitor, never more than $75. Type 2: a generic. A visit’s copay each January, April, July and October.
Arthritis
A generic each fill, and a visit’s copay in about two months of twelve (estimated)
A Course Of Therapy
8 weekly sessions: 50 minutes at Yale Mental Health & Counseling, free to a student Yale Health covers; or 60 minutes at Adna Linden Psychotherapy, $240 a session whatever your cover, its full fee, paid from your bank as each is held, and billed as care where the bank can’t
Time
Each session on the calendar at 5:00 PM on a weekday (estimated)
What Happens
STRAIGHT AWAY
Keep It Up: this month’s care is paid at once from your checking account, then the easy-access savings at its bank where Savings Covers The Current Account is On, then its overdraft. If it can’t be, the row says the care went unpaid. The toast says “Kept up from this month.”
Let It Go: care and refills stop at once, and the toast says “Care stopped. It’s left untreated from now on.”
Begin A Course Of 8 Sessions: the first session is set a week later, at 5:00 PM on a weekday, and the toast gives its date. While it runs, depression’s monthly therapy charge stops; each session is paid as it’s held.
LATER ON
On the first of each month, each kept-up condition’s care is paid. If the bank can’t cover it, the condition goes without and counts as left untreated until the next month.
Each Monday, medicine with 7 days or fewer left is refilled for 30 days, and a condition left untreated or out of medicine takes its toll.
Each session at its hour: awake and out of hospital, it’s held, and paid or billed; asleep or in hospital, it moves to the next week. After the last, the depression lifts at the course’s rate or stays, and another course can be had.
Yale Mental Health & Counseling sees students Yale Health covers: if that cover ends mid-course, the course ends with it, and the sessions had stay had. Adna Linden Psychotherapy can then begin a new course of 8, at its fee.
READING THE RESULT
“The Depression Has Lifted” takes it off your record: no more care, medicine or weekly loss of morale. “The Course Is Done” means it stayed.
Out Of Medicine means the supply ran out: the condition counts as left untreated until Monday’s fill.
Care and medicine for a condition are paid straight from your bank, so they show on your statements, not as rows in Care And Its Bills.
How It Connects
CHANGES STRAIGHT AWAY
Your Accounts: Keep It Up pays the month’s care at once from your checking account, then the easy-access savings at its bank where Savings Covers The Current Account is On, then its overdraft; later months and each fill are paid the same way.
CHANGES LATER
How You Are: Each Monday a long-term condition left untreated takes its toll: depression lowers morale, diabetes your condition, arthritis your energy.
The Calendar: Begin A Course Of 8 Sessions puts a session on the calendar each week, a commitment the clock stops at.
The Doctor And The Pharmacy: A condition kept up books its review as a doctor’s appointment when it falls due.
WHAT LEADS HERE
How You Are: Long-term conditions are kept up or let go on Papers, and your own page says which.
Health Cover: A condition’s month of care and each fill of its medicine are priced at your plan’s copays.
The Doctor And The Pharmacy: Your Pharmacy’s cash price is read for every generic fill of a condition’s medicine.
What To Do Next
Keep enough in your checking account on the first of each month for each condition’s care.
With depression, begin a course of therapy early in your time at the School, while Yale Health covers it.
If You Can’t
“You don’t have that.”: a condition you don’t have.
“Choose a therapist where you live.”, “A course of therapy here is for depression.” or “You’re in a course already.”
“Yale Mental Health & Counseling sees students Yale Health covers.” After Yale Health, Adna Linden Psychotherapy takes a course in New Haven, at $240 a session.
MISTAKES, AND PUTTING THEM RIGHT
Letting a condition go to save money: the weekly toll keeps coming, and type 1 diabetes left untreated makes the emergency room 4 times as likely, each visit billed.
Missing sessions: each one missed asleep or in hospital moves the course a week.
Starting late in your last year: if Yale Health ends before the last session, the course at Yale ends there, and finishing means a new course of 8 at Adna Linden Psychotherapy, at $240 a session. Begin early.
What Decides It
How Often A Life Begins With One
At the rates for adults 18 to 34: depression 25%, asthma 10.1%, high blood pressure 11.5%, diabetes 2% and arthritis 5%. Diabetes, high blood pressure and arthritis can also begin later, likelier in a heavier body
Kept Up
Treated, with this month’s care paid and the medicine not run out: all three at once
Left Untreated, Each Week
Depression takes 3 morale, diabetes 2 condition, arthritis 2 energy; asthma makes an emergency 2 times as likely, and type 1 diabetes 4 times; high blood pressure does nothing a year shows (estimated)
A Course’s Chance
36% for a private course or Yale’s, 48.5% for NHS Talking Therapies (estimated)
Reviews
A doctor’s visit booked for a condition kept up: high blood pressure and asthma every 12 months, diabetes every 6
A Worked Example

A first-year on Yale Health who carries depression.

Open Papers, Health Cover. Depression reads Kept Up, with its medicine’s date.
Choose Yale Mental Health & Counseling, Free With Yale Health, and press Begin A Course Of 8 Sessions.
Be awake and out of hospital at 5:00 PM on each session’s day.

What comes of it. Each session costs $0. After the last, 36% of the time a notice says “The Depression Has Lifted”, and depression is gone from Your Long-Term Conditions; otherwise “The Course Is Done”, and another course can begin.
