Unemployment And Assistance
Fold It Up

Unemployment insurance pays you each week when you’re out of work, and SNAP helps pay for food. On the Unemployment tab, File A Claim opens a claim with Connecticut, where you earn your wages: from $44 ($45 from 2027) to $721 a week, by what you earned, for up to 26 weeks, with no waiting week. Connecticut doesn’t pay a full-time student, so a claim waits until you’ve left school. Apply, on the SNAP panel, puts up to $306 a month of food assistance on an EBT card, and each day’s groceries are paid from it first.

Where To Find It
Papers, Unemployment: SNAP And Your Claim.
When You Can Use It
From the guide’s chapter “Cover, Benefits And Returns”.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Papers, then Unemployment.
The claim panel, No Claim Open, says what filing now would pay, or why it wouldn’t. File A Claim shows beside its title only when a claim would pay.
Once filed, the panel is A Connecticut Claim: A Week, Paid, and At Most, with the date the claim ends.
On the SNAP panel, press Apply when it shows. Claim, At Most and On The EBT Card follow the case.
What You Need First
A claim: covered wages in your base period, at least 40 times the weekly benefit (the Summer Cabaret’s stipend counts; work-study never does); no claim open; out of school; and US citizenship or permission to work, such as OPT.
SNAP: US citizenship, being an adult, and no case open; in the summer recess while you’re at school, 87 hours of work in the last 30 days.
TIME AND MONEY
Time
None: filing and applying move no clock
Money
None. What a claim pays is income on your return.
What Happens
STRAIGHT AWAY
File A Claim: the claim opens, the toast says “Claim filed: …” with its weekly amount, and the first week is certified the coming Sunday.
Apply: the SNAP case opens, and the toast gives the day the first month comes.
LATER ON
Each Sunday at 8 in the evening the week is certified. In the US, out of school, allowed to work, and out of hospital and not laid up for most of the week’s days, you’re paid the benefit less two-thirds of the week’s pay, into the account your payments go to.
The claim closes when it has paid its most, or a year after filing, with the notice “Your Unemployment Claim Ended”.
SNAP’s month is worked out a week after applying, then every 30 days, and what’s due goes onto the EBT card with the notice “SNAP Paid”. Under the state’s gross limit every month but the first pays at least SNAP’s least, $25 from October 1, 2026; the first, or a month over the limit, whose income leaves nothing due pays nothing and says nothing.
A student in the summer recess without the hours has the case closed, with a notice; apply again once that changes.
Out of school and past the time limit, SNAP pays nothing, and says so each month, until you work the hours. While you’re at school, or while an unemployment claim is open, the time limit doesn’t apply.
READING THE RESULT
A Week is the claim’s benefit, Paid what it has paid, and At Most where it stops, with the date it ends.
For a sense of size: a summer with the company paying $1,500 in June and $3,375 in July and August makes a week’s benefit of $93, and $2,418 at most.
On The EBT Card is what’s left for groceries: each morning’s groceries come off it before your bank.
Past Claims keeps each closed claim, its base period and what it paid.
How It Connects
COMES FIRST
Cabaret And Summer Cabaret: The Summer Cabaret’s stipend is the pay a claim counts: its quarters are your base period’s wages.
Your Standing And Classes: A Connecticut claim pays only once you’ve left school: graduated, withdrawn or dismissed.
CHANGES LATER
Looking After Yourself: Each month’s SNAP goes onto the EBT card, and each morning’s groceries are paid from it first.
COUNTS TOWARD
Work-Study Shifts: In the summer recess, a student’s hours of work in the last 30 days, work-study’s among them, are read against SNAP’s 87; work-study’s pay isn’t counted as income, and at school SNAP’s time limit doesn’t apply.
KEPT IN YOUR RECORD
Your Tax Return: What a claim pays is kept as the year’s unemployment insurance, income on your return.
WHAT LEADS HERE
Permission To Work: Unemployment insurance pays a noncitizen only with permission to work in the US, such as OPT in force.
What To Do Next
Once a claim is open, stay in New Haven and out of hospital on Sundays, when each week is certified.
In the summer recess, keep 20 hours of work a week if you want SNAP to stay open.
If You Can’t
“Connecticut treats a full-time student as not available for work (CGS 31-235(b)), so a claim pays only once you’ve left school.”
“Unemployment pays a noncitizen only with permission to work in the US, such as OPT (FUTA 3304(a)(14)).”
“Connecticut asks for base-period wages of 40 times the weekly benefit: …”, followed by what your base period’s quarters paid.
“You already have a claim open.”
“In the game, SNAP is only for US citizens, because a noncitizen’s eligibility depends on immigration details the game doesn’t track.”
“A student in the summer without work-study or 20 hours of work a week isn’t eligible for SNAP (7 CFR 273.5).”
Universal Credit, Jobseeker’s Allowance, EI Special Benefits with its Register, Ontario Works and Income Assistance show only for a life living in Britain, Ireland or Canada, and the Seguro De Desempleo takes no new claim at all. A life begun now lives in New Haven, so their panels don’t show.
MISTAKES, AND PUTTING THEM RIGHT
Counting on work-study to qualify a claim: Yale’s pay to its own student is outside the base period. The Summer Cabaret’s stipend is what counts.
Filing while still enrolled: Connecticut refuses it. File once you’ve graduated, withdrawn or been dismissed.
Spending the summer recess without work: a student’s SNAP case closes. Join The Summer Company, or apply again in the fall.
Being in hospital or laid up for most of a week: that week pays nothing.
What Decides It
The Base Period
The first four of the last five completed quarters, or, where those fall short, the last four
Connecticut’s Week
The two highest quarters’ average over 26, down to the dollar, at least $44 in 2026 and $45 from 2027, estimated by the statute’s index, and at most $721; 26 weeks’ worth at most, or a year from filing
A Week With Work
The benefit less two-thirds of the week’s pay, rounded up to the dollar: nothing once the pay reaches one and a half times the benefit
SNAP’s Month
Up to $306 from October 1, 2026, less 30% of net income rounded up to the dollar: last month’s wages and unearned income, less 20% of the wages and a $217 deduction. Work-study pay isn’t counted. Under the state’s gross limit, never less than $25 after the first month.
SNAP’s Time Limit
Out of school, aged 18 to 64, with under 80 hours’ work in the last 30 days: 3 months in 36. A student at school is exempt, through the summer recess too, and so is anyone with an unemployment claim open
A Worked Example

A US citizen who graduated in the spring, whose base period holds a summer with the Summer Cabaret: $1,500 in June and $3,375 in July and August.

Open Papers, Unemployment. No Claim Open reads “Filed now, your base period, …, pays …”.
Press File A Claim.
Stay in New Haven, out of hospital, through Sunday evening.

What comes of it. The toast says “Claim filed: $93.00 a week.” Each Sunday $93 goes into your account, with no waiting week first, until $2,418 has been paid or a year has passed; it’s income on your return.

Pensions
Fold It Up

Social Security pays a monthly benefit on your US earnings record: 40 credits qualify, one for each $1,890 of covered wages, four a year at most. Claim Social Security from 62 for a cut benefit, 70% of it at 62, the full one at 67, or more by waiting, 124% at 70. At school, your only covered work is the Summer Cabaret, a credit or two a summer, so your record grows only that far. Britain’s, Ireland’s and Mexico’s pensions have panels of their own, shown only if your record or citizenship qualifies for them.

Where To Find It
Papers, Unemployment: Social Security And The State Pensions.
When You Can Use It
From the guide’s chapter “Cover, Benefits And Returns”. Social Security’s panel shows once your US work has earned a credit.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Papers, then Unemployment. The pension panels sit above the claim panel.
Social Security shows Credits, At 67, A Month (with what 62 and 70 would pay) and Claimed.
Claim Social Security shows beside its title once you can claim. The toast gives the monthly amount and its share of the full benefit.
Each other pension has its own panel and Claim It: State Pension, State Pension (Ireland), IMSS Pension and Pensión Para El Bienestar.
What You Need First
Social Security: 62 or older, 40 credits, and not drawing it.
State Pension, the UK’s: State Pension age, 68 for anyone born after April 5, 1978, and 10 qualifying years on your National Insurance record.
State Pension (Ireland): 66, and 520 paid contributions, or living in Ireland with means under the non-contributory pension’s.
IMSS Pension: 65, and the year’s weeks of IMSS contributions, 875 in 2026 and 25 more each year to 1,000.
Pensión Para El Bienestar: a Mexican citizen of 65 or over, living in Mexico.
TIME AND MONEY
Time
None: claiming moves no clock
Money
None to claim. A claim stands for life: it can’t be taken back or made again.
What Happens
STRAIGHT AWAY
Claim Social Security: the month’s amount is fixed from your record and your age that day, and the toast says it.
Claim It on another pension: claimed from today, and the toast gives its week, month or two months.
LATER ON
Social Security is paid a month after claiming and every month after, into the account your payments go to, with a notice. It’s income on your return.
The UK’s State Pension comes every four weeks, Ireland’s every week, the IMSS pension every month, and the Pensión para el Bienestar every two months while you live in Mexico.
READING THE RESULT
Credits says “You need forty to qualify, and years at school earn only a few”. At $375 a week, a summer’s stipend of about 13 weeks earns 2; four a year is the most any year can earn.
At 67, A Month is what today’s record would pay; a later, better year replaces a lower one among your best 35.
A life born in Mexico, a Mexican citizen by its Place Of Birth, sees the Pensión Para El Bienestar panel, and living in New Haven it reads “It’s only for Mexican citizens living in Mexico.”
How It Connects
COMES FIRST
Cabaret And Summer Cabaret: The Summer Cabaret’s stipend, with FICA withheld, is the work that earns a school life its credits.
CHANGES LATER
Your Accounts: Once claimed, each payment goes into the account your payments go to, on its own day.
COUNTS TOWARD
Permission To Work: A year as a nonresident on an F-1 earns no credit: your status is read for each year of your record.
KEPT IN YOUR RECORD
Your Tax Return: A pension paid is kept as the year’s pension income, and Social Security is taxed on the return as IRC 86 says.
If You Can’t
“You can claim it from 62. It’s full at 67, and more if you wait until 70.”
“It takes forty credits to qualify, and your US work has earned …”
“You’ve already claimed it.”
The UK’s, Ireland’s and the IMSS panels show only with a record there: UK earnings, Irish contributions, IMSS days. A life begun now works only in New Haven, so they stay hidden.
MISTAKES, AND PUTTING THEM RIGHT
Claiming at 62 when you could wait: the cut lasts for life. At 62 you keep 70% of the full benefit; at 70, 124%.
Counting work-study toward credits: a student working for their own school pays no FICA, and earns none.
What Decides It
Covered Wages
Each year’s US wages to its taxable maximum, less work-study, which pays no FICA; a year as a nonresident on an F-1 counts nothing. The Summer Cabaret’s stipend counts.
The Benefit At 67
Your best 35 years, indexed to the year you turn 60 and averaged a month, then 90%, 32% and 15% across $1,286 and $7,749
Early Or Late
Cut 5/9 of 1% a month for the first 36 months early and 5/12 of 1% after; raised 8% a year to 70
After 2026
Where SSA hasn’t published the wage index, the maximum, the bend points or the credit yet, the game uses its latest figures (estimated)
A Worked Example

A US citizen in the fall of their third year, after two summers with the Summer Cabaret.

Open Papers, Unemployment.
Read the Social Security panel.

What comes of it. Credits reads 4, against the 40 that qualify, and Claimed reads Not Yet, with “You can claim it from 62. It’s full at 67, and more if you wait until 70.” under it. With no covered work after school in the game, the record stops near there, and Claim Social Security never shows for this life.

Passport And ID
Fold It Up

Your passport and your state ID card prove who you are. A bank you don’t bank with yet asks to see one of them in force before it opens an account. The Social Security office asks for your passport, and so does the DMV if you’re not a US citizen. Applying for one isn’t the same as holding it: it counts only once it’s issued and arrives. On Passport And ID you apply for or renew each one, report a lost or stolen paper, and replace a license or an ID card.

Where To Find It
Papers, Passport And ID, Your Passport And Your ID.
When You Can Use It
From the guide’s chapter “Passports And ID”. File A Police Report opens with “Cover, Benefits And Returns”.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Papers, then the Passport And ID tab. Your Passport shows the one in force, A New One with its fee and wait, and Faster where the office offers it.
Press Apply For One, or Renew It if you hold one. Apply Faster or Renew It Faster pays for the quicker service.
Under Your ID, press Get and the card’s name, such as Get Non-Driver Identification Card.
If a passport, license, international driving permit or ID card in force is lost, press Report Lost… or Report Stolen… in its row, then Cancel It to confirm, or Keep It to back out.
In the same row, press File A Police Report where the police take one online, and Replace It for a license or an ID card.
Press a paper’s name, number or status to open it: who issued it, when it runs out, and what it lets you do today.
What You Need First
A passport office for your citizenship that the game has, and no application already in.
For the ID card: living where the game issues one (New York, Connecticut, California, Ontario, British Columbia, Mexico City or Ireland), with no license from there in force and no card held or on its way.
If you’re not a US citizen, at a US state’s counter: being in status; being at school on an F-1, or, once school is over, holding a US permit in force such as OPT; a primary identity document in force (your passport, or OPT’s card instead); and a Social Security number, which the game issues only through work-study at school.
To replace a card: report it lost first, and live where it was issued (though New York mails a license out of state).
Enough in your bank for the fee.
TIME AND MONEY
Time
None: applying, reporting and replacing don’t move the clock
A US Passport
$165 the first time or after one is lost, ready in up to 42 days, good for 10 years. Renewed by mail on Form DS-82, it’s $130, if your most recent passport was issued within 15 years, at 16 or older, and never reported lost. $60 more gets it in 21 days
Another Country’s Passport
Applied for from New Haven, so from abroad: its office’s fee and time for an applicant outside the country, where the game has them, such as the UK’s £116.50 online, Australia’s A$611 with its overseas surcharge, and Japan’s $62 at a consulate in the US. Its faster service is offered only where it’s sold abroad, which the UK’s Fast Track isn’t. Where an office’s own figure couldn’t be read, the fine print says what the game assumes: New Zealand’s GST (charged), and its urgent fee from overseas, taken as its standard fee (estimated)
Connecticut’s ID Card
$28, good for 7 years, to your first birthday at least 7 years on. It’s mailed, and comes 20 business days after you apply, not counting weekends and federal holidays. If you’re not a citizen, the DMV’s SAVE check comes first, 10 federal workdays, and the card runs to your program’s end while you’re at school, or on OPT to the end printed on it, 12 months from its start. That term is assumed, because the state publishes no term for a card it doesn’t verify. If OPT is canceled for its days without work, the card stays in force to that printed end (estimated)
Replacing An ID Card
Connecticut $30 in 30 days; New York $8 in 21; California $40 in 28
Replacing A License
Connecticut $30 in 30 days; New York $17.50 in 21, free if it was stolen and the police have your report; California $37 in 28
A Police Report
Free, and filed at once
What Happens
STRAIGHT AWAY
The fee leaves your bank, and a passport you’ve applied for shows Being Decided with the day it should be ready. You don’t hold it yet.
Connecticut’s ID card shows On Its Way until it comes by mail, 20 business days later. If you’re not a citizen, it shows Being Decided first, during the DMV’s SAVE check. Until it comes, you can’t show it as a photo ID.
Reported lost or stolen, a paper is canceled for good, even if it turns up. A passport takes with it any visa or travel authorization issued on it, though an F-1 status continues.
A police report is kept on the lost paper’s record.
Replace It cancels the lost card and puts a new one, with a new number, on its way.
LATER ON
A passport is issued on its day for its term, and the one it replaces is canceled then, along with any travel authorization on it.
A new or replacement card arrives on its day, and you can use it from then. Until it comes, you can’t show it as a photo ID.
READING THE RESULT
Status in a row reads In Force, Being Decided, On Its Way (an ID card past every check, in the mail), Reported Lost, Canceled or Run Out.
A license that has run out says beside it that you can’t renew a driving license in the game, and to use a passport or ID card in force as your photo ID. A passport or ID card that has run out says to apply for a new one in its panel. A new bank asks for one in force.
A passport’s own page counts the countries that would let you in on it for a week’s visit. That’s for reference only: travel isn’t part of the game, so you never cross a border.
A card’s own page says “It meets REAL ID.” on a US state ID card issued to a citizen, and “It’s marked Not For Federal Identification: it isn’t REAL ID.” on one issued to someone who isn’t, as Connecticut issues it. A license you began with says “It meets REAL ID.” if it was drawn as one: at its state’s published share of REAL ID licenses, or, for a state with none published, the average of the shares that are. There are no flights in the game, so no airport check reads it.
Going Abroad lists what each country asks of a short-stay visitor with your citizenship, for reference. You can’t apply for visas or travel authorizations here.
In New Haven a police report is kept on the record, and nothing else there reads it. New York’s free replacement of a stolen license is the rule that reads one.
How It Connects
COMES FIRST
Permission To Work: On an F-1, Connecticut’s DMV asks for your Social Security number before it issues an ID card.
Permission To Work: If you’re not a citizen, Connecticut’s DMV asks for your passport in force, or OPT’s card, before it issues an ID card.
CHANGES STRAIGHT AWAY
Your Accounts: Each fee leaves your accounts when you apply or replace.
COUNTS TOWARD
Another Bank: A bank you don’t bank with yet checks your passport, license or ID card before it opens an account or takes your switch.
Permission To Work: The Social Security office asks for your passport in force before it takes an application.
WHAT LEADS HERE
Another Bank: A new bank asks for a valid photo ID: a passport, a driver’s license or an ID card.
Permission To Work: The Social Security office asks for your passport in force.
Residence Abroad: A citizenship by naturalizing joins the one you were born with, and your passport stays your birth country’s.
What To Do Next
If you’re not a US citizen and want a state ID card, get your Social Security number first: see Permission To Work.
Keep at least one photo ID in force before you open an account at a new bank.
If You Can’t
“Your country’s passport office isn’t in the game.” or “You’ve already applied, and it’s being decided.”
Apply Faster shows only where the office offers a faster service to you where you are. From abroad, where it offers none, the refusal says “… offers no faster service to applicants abroad.” Where that service “is for renewals only”, it waits until you’ve held a passport from that office.
Get, if you’re not a US citizen and have no passport in force and no OPT card: “The DMV asks for a primary identity document in force: your passport, with your I-94 and I-20. Apply for a passport or renew it under Your Passport first.”
Get: “You hold a driving license from here, and it already serves as your ID.”, “You already hold one in force.”, “One is already on its way.”, or, if you live where the game issues no card, the list of places it does.
Get, if you’re not a US citizen, at a US state’s counter: “The DMV checks lawful presence through SAVE, and you’re out of status, so it won’t issue you a card.” Out of school on an F-1 with no OPT in force: “On an F-1, the DMV asks for your I-20 and proof that you’re enrolled, and you’re not at school.” With no Social Security number: “The DMV asks for your Social Security number, or the SSA’s letter that you can’t have one.”, followed by where you stand. At school: “You can get one through work-study: apply for it first, under Social Security Number on Papers.” Applied for: “Yours is on its way.” Out of school with none applied for: “In the game, the number goes only to an F-1 student at school, through work-study, and the letter is never issued.”, so the card is out of reach.
Report Lost… and Report Stolen… show only on a passport, a license, an international driving permit or an ID card in force. A visa, a permit or a travel authorization is a status the government holds, and losing its paper doesn’t end it.
File A Police Report: “Here lost property is reported in person at a police station, not online.” or “Here a theft is reported in person at a police station, not online.”
Replace It, for an ID card: “It’s replaced only where it was issued, for someone living there.” If it has run out, or runs out before a new card would come: “It ran out on …” or “It runs out on …, before a new card would come”, then “, and a replacement keeps the same date, so it can’t be replaced. Apply for a new card instead, if you can.”
Replace It, for a license from elsewhere: “Its issuer replaces it only for someone living there, and no way to send one out of state was found.” Only New York’s issuer mails one out of state, on its form MV-44, so a New York license is replaced from New Haven.
Replace It, for a license that has run out or runs out before a new card would come: “It ran out on …” or “It runs out on …, before a new card would come”, then that a replacement keeps the same date, and a license past its date has to be renewed instead, which the game doesn’t offer.
Either way, where the game doesn’t have the issuer’s fee: “What its issuer charges to replace it isn’t in the game.”
Any fee: “Your bank can’t cover …, so nothing was charged.”
MISTAKES, AND PUTTING THEM RIGHT
Reporting a paper lost by mistake: it can’t be undone, so the second press, Cancel It, is the one that counts. Keep It backs out.
Replacing a stolen New York license before filing the police report: the free replacement reads the report, and once it’s replaced, the lost license’s row offers no report. File it first.
Letting your only photo ID lapse before switching banks: the new bank refuses until one is in force. A license from home runs out and can’t be renewed in the game, so get the ID card where you live instead.
Reporting your passport lost before getting the ID card when you’re not a citizen: the DMV asks for your passport as your identity document, so the card waits on a new passport from your office, which takes weeks from abroad.
Asking Connecticut for an ID card on an F-1 before you have your Social Security number: the DMV asks for it, and the game issues the number only through work-study at school, so apply under Permission To Work while you’re registered. A graduate on OPT who never applied is turned away for good.
What Decides It
Your Citizenship
Which passport office you apply to, and its fee, wait and term
Your Age
A shorter passport where the office gives one to a young adult; a lower fee to replace an ID card in New York and California from 62
Where You Live
Which state’s ID card you can get, whether the police take a report online, and where a card is replaced
A Photo ID In Force
A bank you don’t bank with yet checks it before it opens an account or takes your switch
A Worked Example

A US citizen in New Haven loses a wallet holding a Connecticut Non-Driver Identification Card.

In the card’s row, press Report Stolen…, then Cancel It.
Press File A Police Report: New Haven’s police take one online.
Press Replace It, $30.

What comes of it. The old card is canceled, with the report kept on it. $30 leaves the bank, and the new card, with a new number, arrives 30 days later. Until then, a passport or a license in force is your photo ID. Without one, a new bank would turn you away.

Permission To Work
Fold It Up

On an F-1, you make two applications here. The first is a Social Security number, which you apply for in person at New Haven’s office. With it, the IRS decides a payment plan at once, some banks open your account online, Connecticut’s DMV can issue you an ID card, and a 1040-NR doesn’t wait on an ITIN. The second is OPT, after your degree, which keeps your US status going past its 60-day grace period. The game has no work after the degree, so OPT ends after 90 days without work.

Where To Find It
Papers, Permission To Work, Social Security Number And OPT.
When You Can Use It
From the guide’s chapter “Passports And ID”. It’s for a student on an F-1: a US citizen already has a Social Security number, and OPT is only for F-1 students.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Papers, then the Permission To Work tab. The Permission To Work panel shows Your Program Ends and Your US Status.
Once you’re registered at the School and have your passport in force, press Apply At The Social Security Office under Social Security Number. It takes an hour there.
From 90 days before your program ends to 60 days after, press Apply For OPT under OPT, or Apply With Premium Processing for a decision within 30 business days.
When your status is ending and you can still apply for OPT, What Needs You asks too, with Apply For OPT and Apply For OPT, Premium Processing.
What You Need First
Being a student on an F-1.
For the number: being registered for your program, since the School’s work-study is the on-campus work it needs; a passport in force; and an hour free, out of hospital.
For OPT: your degree completed or on its way, applying inside its window, and no OPT applied for before.
OPT’s fee in your accounts.
TIME AND MONEY
Time
60 minutes at the Social Security office, and the clock moves on by that much. Applying for OPT doesn’t move the clock (estimated)
A Social Security Number
Free
OPT
$470 filed online; premium processing costs $1,780 more
How Long
The card comes in 21 days. OPT is decided in 90 days, or within 30 business days with premium processing, not counting weekends and federal holidays (estimated)
What Happens
STRAIGHT AWAY
Applying for the number moves the clock an hour and puts the card on its way, with its date under Social Security Number.
Applying for OPT takes the fee and lists Employment Authorization, OPT, as Being Decided. You don’t hold it until it’s approved. The status item in What Needs You is answered.
While OPT is being decided, your status holds, past its grace period if need be.
LATER ON
The card arrives on its day. A bank that opens accounts online for people with a number can now open one for you.
If OPT is approved, it runs for 12 months from the later of your program’s end and the approval.
On OPT, each week without work counts. After 90 days in total, OPT ends, and your status with it, with no grace period.
When your permission has run out and only the grace period is left, What Needs You says Your US Status Is Ending, with its date.
If you stay past it, you’re out of status. In the game, that cancels your F-1 visa, ends a marketplace plan at the end of the month, closes Covered Connecticut and the DMV’s ID card to you, and closes the Visa Waiver Program to you from then on.
READING THE RESULT
Your US Status reads Held while you study or an application is being decided; Ends with its date once school is over and nothing is being decided (on OPT, the day its days without work run out, with no grace period after); or Out Of Status.
An approved OPT reads In Force with its dates, and Canceled once its days without work have run out.
The game keeps no actual Social Security number, only whether you hold one, so no number is shown.
How It Connects
COMES FIRST
Orientation Week: You need to be registered for your program to get the number: once you are, the School’s work-study counts as your on-campus work.
Passport And ID: The Social Security office asks for your passport in force.
CHANGES LATER
Health Cover: Your status ends on a set day. Once you’re out of status, a marketplace plan ends at the end of the month.
COUNTS TOWARD
Your Tax Return: A 1040-NR filed without a number goes in with an ITIN application, which holds up its refund seven weeks longer.
Payment Plans And Waivers: With a number, the IRS decides a plan within a minute. Without one, it’s by mail in 30 days.
Another Bank: Without a number, a bank that opens accounts for international students opens yours only in a branch.
Unemployment And Assistance: Unemployment insurance pays a noncitizen only with permission to work in the US, such as OPT in force.
WHAT LEADS HERE
What Needs You: When your US status is ending, its question carries Apply For OPT while that can still be applied for.
Leave, Withdrawal And Coming Back: On an F-1, a medical leave extends the I-20 a year once it begins, and withdrawing leaves 15 days’ grace and no OPT.
Repeating, Extra Terms And Incompletes: On an F-1, a repeat or an additional term extends the I-20 a year when it’s granted.
Pensions: A year as a nonresident on an F-1 earns no credit: your status is read for each year of your record.
Your Tax Return: On a 1040-NR, having a Social Security number before you file saves the seven weeks an ITIN application holds up the refund.
Payment Plans And Waivers: A Social Security number gets an IRS plan decided within a minute. Without one it takes 30 days.
Passport And ID: The Social Security office asks for your passport in force before it takes an application.
Passport And ID: On an F-1, Connecticut’s DMV asks for your Social Security number before it issues an ID card.
Passport And ID: If you’re not a citizen, Connecticut’s DMV asks for your passport in force, or OPT’s card, before it issues an ID card.
Residence Abroad: Residence abroad and permission to work in the US are separate: OPT is the US route for a student.
What To Do Next
Once the card comes, a new bank can open an account for you online, and Connecticut’s DMV can issue you an ID card: see Passport And ID.
Near your program’s end, apply for OPT inside its window if you want your status to last past the grace period.
If You Can’t
The number’s button shows only while you have no number and none on its way. A US citizen’s panel reads Held, as a US citizen.
“On an F-1, you can get a number only with on-campus work that has started or starts within 30 days. Register at the School first: once you’re registered, the School’s work-study counts.”, or once school is over, “On an F-1, you can get a number only with on-campus work, and yours ended with your program.”
“The office asks for your passport, and you don’t have one in force.”, or another commitment in that hour.
OPT: “You can apply from …”, a date 90 days before your program ends, or “The time to apply closed on …”, 60 days after.
“OPT follows a completed degree, and you left without one.”
“You’ve already applied for OPT.”, once, even after it ends; and for a US citizen, “OPT is for a student on an F-1, and you’re a US citizen.”
MISTAKES, AND PUTTING THEM RIGHT
Waiting for the card before working shifts: work-study pays without it, because the IRS lets an employer report the number as applied for.
Leaving the number until after your degree: once school is over the office refuses it, and without it Connecticut’s DMV won’t issue you an ID card, even on OPT. One applied for in your program’s last weeks still comes.
Counting on OPT’s 12 months: with no work after the degree in the game, it ends after its days without work. What it gives you here is those days in status, and with them the marketplace, and unemployment insurance if your wages qualify.
Paying for premium processing to keep your status: your status holds while either kind is being decided, so the $1,780 only buys an earlier answer. If that answer comes after your program’s end, OPT starts sooner, and with no work its days run out sooner too.
What Decides It
Your Program’s End
May 31 of your class’s last year, or the day you left school without the degree
How School Ended
The grace period after your program: 60 days with the degree, 15 after a withdrawal or a degree withheld, and none after a dismissal. OPT follows a completed degree: if you applied while the degree was on its way and school ends without it, OPT is denied when it’s decided, and the fee isn’t refunded
Your Registration
The number needs on-campus work that has started or starts within 30 days. Once you’re registered, the School’s work-study counts
Days Without Work
Counted on OPT a week at a time. After 90, OPT ends
A Worked Example

An F-1 student in the class that began in 2026, whose program ends May 31, 2029, with no work lined up.

On March 3, 2029, press Apply For OPT.
Graduate, and stay in New Haven.

What comes of it. $470 leaves the bank. OPT is decided on June 1, 2029 and runs from June 1, 2029. With no work, it ends on August 31, 2029, past its 90 days, and your status ends with it. Without OPT, your status would have ended on July 30, 2029.

Residence Abroad
Fold It Up

Residence Abroad lists Canada, Ireland, Mexico, Britain and the United States, apart from your own country, with your status in each: what the country asks, and why the game grants none of it. Mexico’s temporary residence asks only for savings or income, but moving abroad isn’t part of the game, so none of Mexico’s papers are granted. What an older save holds is kept: a card to its end, and an application for citizenship to its decision.

Where To Find It
Papers, Permission To Work, Residence Abroad.
When You Can Use It
From the guide’s chapter “Passports And ID”. A country you’re a citizen of, by birth or naturalized, leaves the list.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Papers, then Permission To Work, and find the Residence Abroad panel. Your Status There says what each country asks, or what you hold there. Mexico’s Apply, and Renew on a card held, are grayed out with the reason.
If an older save holds Britain’s Global Talent visa or a green card, press Settle or Naturalize where they show.
What You Need First
There’s nothing to apply for: each country’s row says why there’s no route. For reference, Mexico’s rule asks for savings of MXN 1,344,373, or an income of MXN 79,771 a month over six months.
To settle or naturalize: residence held from an older save, without a break, for the years the country asks.
TIME AND MONEY
Time
None
Mexico’s Fees
MXN 11,140.74 a year for the card and $56 for the consulate’s visa, MXN 13,578.96 for permanent residence and MXN 9,502.01 to naturalize. These are shown with its rule, and nothing here charges them
What Happens
STRAIGHT AWAY
Your Status There gives each country’s answer, and nothing leaves your bank.
Settle (Britain) or Naturalize, where an older save’s papers allow it: the fee leaves your bank, and Your Status There shows what’s granted, or the day citizenship is decided.
LATER ON
A citizenship you’ve applied for is decided on its day. It joins the one you were born with, and its country leaves the list. You keep your birth country’s passport.
A Mexican card an older save holds runs out at its end, and isn’t renewed.
READING THE RESULT
Your Status There gives each country’s answer in its own words: Canada’s paused program, Ireland’s need for an employer’s offer, the professional record Britain and the US would judge, and Mexico’s rule with why the game grants none.
Residence you hold shows its name, and its end date if it has one.
Mexico’s temporary residence would let you live there, but not work, and a life in New Haven never uses it.
How It Connects
CHANGES STRAIGHT AWAY
Your Accounts: Settling or naturalizing, where an older save’s papers allow it, takes its fee from your accounts at once.
WORTH DOING WITH IT
Passport And ID: A citizenship by naturalizing joins the one you were born with, and your passport stays your birth country’s.
Permission To Work: Residence abroad and permission to work in the US are separate: OPT is the US route for a student.
If You Can’t
Mexico’s row: “Mexico grants temporary residence on savings of MXN 1,344,373 or an income of MXN 79,771 a month over six months, with the card at MXN 11,140.74 a year and the consulate’s visa at US$56. Moving abroad isn’t part of the game, so you can’t get Mexico’s papers here.”
A Mexican card held: “Mexico renews temporary residence a year at a time, in the card’s last 30 days, for MXN 11,140.74. Moving abroad isn’t part of the game, so you can’t get Mexico’s papers here.”
Settle and Naturalize show only once they’re allowed. Mexico’s, after their four and five years, say why the game grants none.
For Canada, Ireland, Britain and the United States, Your Status There says why there’s no route.
Any fee: “Your bank can’t cover …, so nothing was charged.”
MISTAKES, AND PUTTING THEM RIGHT
Saving toward Mexico’s savings test in the hope it opens something: it’s Mexico’s rule, shown for reference, and the game grants nothing on it.
What Decides It
Residence Held
Counted from its first grant, each grant reaching the next with no more than a day between
A Record Of Professional Work
What Britain’s Global Talent visa and a US green card are judged on. The game has none to show
A Worked Example

A student from a wealthy family with MXN 1,344,373, about $74,687, in the bank, which meets Mexico’s savings test.

Open Residence Abroad and read Mexico’s row.

What comes of it. Mexico’s row gives its rule, savings of MXN 1,344,373 or an income of MXN 79,771 a month over six months, and says the game grants none of its papers, because moving abroad isn’t part of the game. Apply is grayed out with those words, nothing leaves the bank, and a student without the savings sees the same row.
